documents.title: Two Hundred and Forty Souls
documents.text:
HIGH COUNCIL INVESTIGATION BUREAU
FIELD LEDGER  -  EASTERN AGRICULTURAL HUB (OAKHAVEN)

Total Population (Pre-Operation): 240 Souls.
Viable Resonance Candidates Positively Identified: 3.

  J.  -  age 7.  'Sparked' in the square before witnesses. FIRST PRIORITY.  Collected.
  W. Harrow  -  age 9.  Flame-sympathy, strong.  Collected.
  T. Crisp  -  age 11.  Stone-resonance (the mill).  Scheduled: next wagon.

Local authority: none of note. Elder compliant. Resistance: negligible.

Contingency on completion: one Void-Seed, Level 4, to be placed in the water supply. The resulting Wasting will be reported as a natural surge, to hide our tracks.

- the rest of the page has been torn away -
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the figures, the Void-Seed and "to hide our tracks" are from book1 ch.4; the initials and schedule are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: Sleep Now, Stone and Sky
documents.text:
Sleep now, stone and sky,
the oak will keep the night.
The wheel will turn, the hens will lie,
the lamp will hold its light.

Sleep now, root and rain,
the grey is far away.
What's taken finds its way again
by the turning of the day.

Sleep now, salt and bone,
your name is in the oak.
No one who sleeps is quite alone
while Oakhaven's hearths still smoke.

(Pieced together from Goody Marl, Old Tobin and Hettie Brook.)
documents.canonStatus: The first line is CANON (book1 ch.23, "an old lullaby from Oakhaven"); the rest is GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Acorn Oath
documents.text:
From the chapel book of Oakhaven, the first leaf, copied fair:

We came east with nine ploughs and one sack of seed, and the land took us in.
On the first day we set an acorn in the middle of the square, and swore on it:
that while the oak stands, Oakhaven stands;
that no one who sleeps under it sleeps alone;
that every child born here has their name cut in its roots.

(Below, in a newer hand:) Cut two names at the roots today, for the two the wagon took. The collectors watched us do it. Let them watch. The oak remembers.
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the chapel book and the oath. The Great Oak as the heart of the settlement is CANON (book1 ch.4).

documents.title: By Order of the King
documents.text:
BY ORDER OF CADDOCK, KING OF CROWSFOOT HOLLOW
(copied fair by Hesk, quartermaster, who can write)

One. The hall is the King's. Nobody sits in the King's chair. Nobody sits in it to see what it is like.

Two. Rations are one bowl a day, and what the King says. The Oakhaven grain is the King's grain.

Three. Nobody goes down the North road by daylight. The farmers keep dogs, and the dogs have long memories.

Four. The crown is not tin. Anyone heard saying it is tin stands the Drop for a week.

Five. Pay is owed. Pay will be paid when the King has a kingdom.

- and under it, smaller, in the same hand: Owed to Hesk, nine months. Owed to the company, everything. -
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: Caddock, Hesk and their orders are invented; the Sandthrone company is CANON.

documents.title: A Letter from Hallow's Creek
documents.text:
To Ada Hollin, at Oakhaven, by the carter. (Pay him a penny. He has earned it.)

Ada, don't you fret over the quiet. The east meadow went pale in the night, that's all: grass and fence-posts and the old ram with them, grey as ash and light as paper, and nobody heard a thing. The reeve says it's a blight off the Peaks and will burn itself out by harvest. Oswin says it is no blight, and got his ear clipped for saying so in the yard.

Mother won't leave the house. I've the cart packed all the same. If it comes past the mill-race I'll bring her whether she likes it or not, and we'll come to you down the creek road. Keep a bed aired, and don't let Rowan sell the brindle cow before we've seen her.

Your loving sister,
Bet. Hallow's Creek, the week before the fair.

(Under it, in pencil, in another hand:) No cart came. Nobody came. The carter says there is no road past the milestone now, only grey. Rowan and I are taking the children west to Khaven before it comes to us. Whoever finds this: the east road doesn't go anywhere any more.  - A. H.
documents.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: Hallow's Creek, the first settlement the Wasting took, is CANON (world_bible.md); the letter, Bet, the Hollins and their flight west are GAME-ONLY.

documents.title: The Watch Book
documents.text:
THE WATCHTOWER ON THE EAST ROAD. Each watcher writes the weather, where the grey stands, and their name.

Fair. Grey at the far hedge past Hollin's. No change.  - W. Carder
Rain. Grey at the far hedge. The hedge is grey now too.  - Tobin
Fair. The grey has the hedge and two rows of Hollin's barley. You can't hear the wind in it.  - Edda P.
Overcast. The crows won't fly over it. Counted them. They go round.  - Garet M.
Fair. Hollin's east field gone, all of it, in the one night. Ada Hollin came up and sat with me and didn't say anything.  - Sel H.
Windy. No change. No change is good.  - W. Carder
Fair. It was nearer this morning than last night. I'd swear it. Nobody else will.  - Tobin

(The rest of the page is torn out along the fold, carefully, as if someone meant to keep it.)
documents.canonStatus: GAME-ONLY: the watchtower and its book. The Wasting creeping across the eastern farms, unmaking rather than burning, is CANON (book1 ch.4; world_bible.md).

quests.title: Two Hundred and Forty Souls
quests.summary: Concord collectors hold Oakhaven. Find Mira, drive them off, and learn what their black-iron wagon is for.
quests.complete:
Corwin reads it twice. His hands shake on the second time.

"Two hundred and forty. They counted us like sacks in a barn." He taps the initials. "J. That's the soldier's little brother, the one who made the lamps flicker. They took him first, before any of us understood. W. Harrow is Wren; Sel has not slept since."

He stops at the last line. "T. Crisp. Tam. The miller's boy. It says they're coming back for him."

steps.text: Find Mira inside the Golden Cask.

objectives.text: Find Mira inside the Golden Cask

steps.text: Drive the Concord collectors out of Oakhaven.
steps.say: They were guarding something on the east road, near the grey. A wagon, all black iron. Whatever is in it, they didn't want the village to see.

steps.text: Keep the Tempered Trailblade in hand [I].
Search the black-iron wagon on the east road.

objectives.say: Behind a strongbox in the cage: small manacles on a chain, and a black-bound ledger.

steps.text: Show the ledger to Corwin Ashby, the village elder.

objectives.text: Show the ledger to Corwin Ashby
objectives.say: What is this? ...Give it here. Let me sit down.

quests.title: The Miller's Boy
quests.summary: Speak with the Harrows and the miller, then ask Mira how a boy might be hidden from the Concord.
quests.offer:
"We can't bring back Wren, or the soldier's boy. Not yet. But Tam is still here, sleeping above the millstones."

"Speak to Sel Harrow; she saw the collectors come. Then Aldo Crisp at the mill. He'll not want to hear it. And ask your healer. Healers know which roads are quiet."
quests.complete: "Salt-Menders." Corwin says the word like a prayer and a curse at once. "If they'll take him, then go with my blessing. And may the oak forgive us for needing them."

steps.text: Speak with Sel Harrow, Aldo Crisp, and Mira.

objectives.say: Wren could make a candle flame lean just by looking at it. We thought it was a blessing. We told people. We TOLD people.
Tam hums, and the millstones hum back. I told him to stop. I told him! ...They're coming for him? Then where do I hide a boy in a village with one road?
Then we keep him out of their sight. The Salt-Menders move people the Concord wants. There's a hooded one at the Cask who isn't here for the ale.

quests.title: The Ruts Go West
quests.canonStatus: CANON-EXPANDED: the Bureau's collection of Oakhaven's resonance candidates is canon (book1 ch.4); the route west and the Sandthrone handover at Khaven are GAME-ONLY.
quests.summary: Follow the collectors' ruts along the West road to Khaven Village and find out who took Wren and the soldier's boy.
quests.offer:
"Tam is out of their reach, for now. The other two aren't." Corwin runs his thumb along the ledger's torn edge.

"They didn't keep those children in that cage. They took them west in the night, before you came: narrow wheels, heavy load. The ruts are still cut in the mud past the signpost on the West road. Follow them to Khaven. Someone there will have seen where they went. Khaven folk see everything and say nothing, so be patient with them."
quests.complete: Wenna spits in the dust by the gate. "You want those children back, you'll go through the two sand-men in our square first. And then you'll have to go further, because they didn't keep them here long."

steps.text: Follow the wagon ruts along the West road to Khaven Village.

objectives.say: The ruts are deep here, where the wagon stood a long while by the creek road. Beside them, small bare footprints in the mud; then hoofprints, a great many, going on toward the gate.

steps.text: Ask in Khaven who saw the wagon. Try the hedge-witch by the gate.

objectives.say: The black wagon? It stopped at our gate a fortnight gone, collectors on the box, and Sandthrone riders waiting for it. They lifted two little ones down in chains and paid in coin, and the wagon went back east empty. The sand-men kept the children.

quests.title: Salt in the Tithe
quests.summary: Spoil the Concord's supply cart on the east road so the next wagon is delayed.
quests.offer:
The hood doesn't turn toward you. "Corwin sent you. Good. I don't do favours, but I do arithmetic."

"The collectors eat from a supply cart on the east road. Salt it. Every sack. They'll need a new cart from Ironhold, and a new cart means another week. For the miller's boy, a week is everything."
quests.complete: "Good. Quiet work, well done." For the first time the hood tilts toward you. "You'll hear from us. The Menders remember the ones who don't ask why."

steps.text: Salt the Concord's supply cart on the east road.

objectives.say: The salt hisses into the grain sacks. No one will be eating Concord bread this week.

quests.title: A Dozen for the Oven
quests.summary: Carry Goody Marl's eggs to Hedda Thorne at the bakehouse, west of the green.
quests.offer:
"Oh, you've a strong back. Take these to Hedda at the bakehouse, would you? My knees don't like that path."

"And mind the basket. The speckled ones are Old Speckle's, and she'll know if you crack one."
quests.complete: "Proper eggs! Tell Goody her girls are the only honest things left in this village. Here, for your trouble."

steps.text: Bring the eggs to Hedda Thorne's bakehouse.

objectives.text: Bring the eggs to Hedda Thorne

quests.title: Ash in the Flour
quests.summary: Have the herbalist test Hedda's grey flour, then fetch clean grain from the Harrow barn.
quests.offer:
"Taste that. No, go on." The flour is dry and oddly light, like nothing at all.

"It's been like that since the harvest. Take a twist to Lisbet Crane; she knows what's in things. And if there's clean grain anywhere, it's in the Harrows' barn. They stored early, before the grey came close."
quests.complete: She rubs the Harrow grain between her fingers and closes her eyes. "That's grain. That's real grain." "Tell no one where it came from. If the collectors hear, they'll tithe that too."

steps.text: Take the flour to Lisbet Crane, the herbalist.

objectives.text: Show the flour to Lisbet Crane
objectives.say: Ash. Not wood ash. It isn't anything at all, really. It just takes up room where the flour should be. Don't eat it.

steps.text: Take a sack of clean grain from the Harrow barn.

objectives.text: Clean grain from the Harrow barn

quests.title: Yarrow for Mira
quests.summary: Gather five bunches of yarrow on the open meadows around the village and take them to Mira.
quests.offer:
"Your healer's running short. I can see it in how she holds her hands."

"Yarrow grows on the open meadows outside the fences. Feathery leaves, flat white flowers. Five good bunches, and take them to her yourself. She'd not take them from me; proud, that one."
quests.complete: Mira turns a sprig in her fingers. "Lisbet sent these? ...Of course she did." She almost smiles. "This will keep you standing a while longer."

steps.text: Gather yarrow on the meadows.

quests.title: What the Deer Know
quests.summary: Follow the deer tracks east toward the grey, then check the Moonbell copse on the way home.
quests.offer:
"You've good eyes? Then use them for me. There's a line of deer tracks heading east, toward the grey. They don't come back."

"Follow them as far as you dare, then on your way back look into the Moonbell copse, south of the east road near the village. Tell me what you see. Don't touch anything grey."
quests.complete: Garet listens without blinking. "Stopped mid-stride. Grey at the roots." He spits. "It's not creeping. Creeping is slow. This is... deliberate. Like something is drawing a line."

steps.text: Follow the deer tracks east toward the grey.

objectives.say: The tracks stop mid-stride, as if the deer simply stopped being. Ahead, the grey stands in a line too straight for nature.

steps.text: Look over the Moonbell copse.

objectives.say: Inside the copse the grass is grey at the roots, and the birdsong stops at the treeline.

quests.title: Good Iron
quests.summary: Take back three bars of confiscated iron from the tithe crates near the Concord wagon.
quests.offer:
"They took my bar iron. Called it a tithe. Stacked it in crates by that wagon of theirs like it was theirs to take."

"Three bars. That's all I ask. With three bars I can shoe every horse left in Oakhaven, and put an edge on anything you like."
quests.complete: He weighs each bar in his palm and nods. "Good iron. Oakhaven iron." The forge roars as he works the bellows. "Come back any time your edge wants care."

steps.text: Recover confiscated iron from the tithe crates on the east road.

quests.title: Sleep Now, Stone and Sky
quests.summary: Collect the verses of Oakhaven's old lullaby from Goody Marl, Old Tobin and Hettie Brook.
quests.offer:
"There was a lullaby. Every mother in Oakhaven sang it: 'Sleep now, stone and sky.' I've lost the rest. Age takes things."

"Goody Marl will have a verse. Old Tobin too, if he's sober enough to find it. And Hettie Brook sang it to half the village. If the grey takes us, I want someone to carry it."
quests.complete: He mouths the verses as you say them, and on the last he sings, cracked and quiet. "There. Now it lives in two heads. Keep it. Sing it somewhere green."

steps.text: Gather the verses of the lullaby.

objectives.say: Oh, that one. 'The wheel will turn, the hens will lie, the lamp will hold its light.' My mother sang it to the hens, if you'll believe it.
Ah... 'Sleep now, root and rain, the grey is far away.' It was, once. It was far away once.
The last verse? 'No one who sleeps is quite alone while Oakhaven's hearths still smoke.' Mind you sing it softly.

quests.title: Roots Before Ruin
quests.summary: Bind the three grey-hearted oaks at the edge of the Harrow wood with living vine-cord, so the grey cannot spread through their roots.
quests.offer:
A woman in green and brown steps out of the treeline. Vine moves on her armour as if it breathes.

"The grey has reached three oaks at the wood's edge. It is in their hearts now; I can hear it. If it reaches the roots it walks under the whole wood. Bind them with this cord. It is alive, and the grey hates what is alive."
quests.complete: Warden Ivel lays a palm on the nearest trunk and listens. "Slower. Not stopped, slower." She bows her head. "The Guild will remember you. Matriarch Solari keeps a long list, and it is not all names of enemies."

steps.text: Bind the grey-hearted oaks at the edge of the Harrow wood.

quests.title: The Tin Crown
quests.summary: Go down through Crowsfoot Hollow, the deserters' cave in the north hills, to the hall deep under them, bring down Caddock, their tin-crowned king, and recover what they stole from Oakhaven's farms.
quests.offer:
Wil Carder turns his cap round and round in his hands. "Deserters. Sandthrone, by what's left of the colours, but no captain would own them now. Three nights they've come down the North road and had my barn: the seed-corn for spring, the hams, my da's good boots off the step."

"Garet tracked them up the North road, past my field barn and the wolf woods, to where it gives out under Crowsfoot Ridge. A track goes on west along the foot of the hill and round its heel, and the cave is there: Crowsfoot Hollow, with its mouth turned away from us. There's a band of them dug in, and one in a tin crown who calls himself king. Caddock, they say. Put them out of that hole and bring back what they took. We've nothing left to give the Concord, never mind a king."
quests.complete:
Wil Carder hears you out without a word. When you come to the seed-corn, still in its marked sacks, his shoulders drop.

"Spring, then. We'll have a spring." He looks up the North road at the dark hills. "A king in a hole in the ground, in a tin hat, and all of us too frightened to sleep. I'll have the cart up there at first light."

steps.text: Clear the deserters out of Crowsfoot Hollow: follow the North road to its end, then the track west round the heel of Crowsfoot Ridge. Their king holds a hall deep under the hill.
steps.say: The hollow goes quiet but for dripping water, far down. Whatever they carried off the farms will be at the back of the king's hall.

objectives.say: The tin crown rolls off across the stone and rings to a stop.

steps.text: Recover what the deserters took from Oakhaven's farms.

objectives.say: Under a torn Sandthrone cloak lie the north farms' missing stores: seed-corn in sacks with the Carder mark, a string of hams, three good kettles, a child's wooden horse. You drag it all out to the mouth of the hollow for the carts.

quests.title: A Wallet for Simples
quests.summary: Bring Maud Tanner three grey wolf pelts. Wolves run in the Upper pines and Thornshaw, up the North road past the last fields. She keeps shop by the South road, 9 to 12 and 2 to 6.
quests.offer:
"You've the look of someone who picks things up. Herbs, is it? They'll bruise to nothing loose in a pack."

"Bring me three wolf pelts, whole, not grey at the edges, and I'll cut you a wallet for them. No charge but the hides; what's left over is my profit, and the gods know I need one."
quests.progress: "Three, I said. The wolves won't skin themselves."
quests.complete: Maud turns each pelt to the light and runs a thumb along the edge. "These'll do. Sit. It's an hour's work if Nettie holds the lamp." The wallet she hands you smells of oak bark and smoke. "The offcuts will buy the bread this week. So that's both of us better off."

steps.text: Bring three grey wolf pelts to Maud Tanner at her shop by the South road.

objectives.text: Grey wolf pelts for Maud Tanner
objectives.say: Lay them on the counter, fur down. Let me have a look at what you've brought me.

quests.title: A Strap for the Woodyard
quests.summary: Bring Maud Tanner three hill-deer hides. Deer graze west of the Old Orchard, in the Mastwood and on the slopes under Crowsfoot Ridge at the top of the North road; go quietly (Ctrl) or they're gone. She keeps shop by the South road, 9 to 12 and 2 to 6.
quests.offer:
"Osk Farrow carries his logs on his bare neck all winter, and by the look of your shoulders you've started doing the same."

"Deer hide makes the best strap there is: it gives without stretching. Bring me three and I'll cut you a log-sling. Go quiet in the long grass, mind. A hill deer hears you think."
quests.progress: "Three hides. A deer you've only frightened doesn't count."
quests.complete: Maud spreads the hides over her bench and scrapes one edge with a thumbnail. "Clean kills. Good." She cuts the strap in one long pull of the knife and stitches the cinches while you wait. "Fen will take the offcuts to the yard, and that's tomorrow's bread. Mind your neck."

steps.text: Bring three hill-deer hides to Maud Tanner at her shop by the South road.

objectives.say: Let's see them, then. Hair side up.

quests.title: The Cook's Scrip
quests.summary: Bring Maud Tanner five coney skins. Rabbits run in every field: by Harrow farm, round Brook pond and out past the Cider Barn. She keeps shop by the South road, 9 to 12 and 2 to 6.
quests.offer:
"Flour in one pocket, salt in the next, a joint of something in the third, and none of it touching. That's a larder-scrip. Hob at the Cask has been after one since the spring."

"Coney skins line it: soft, and they don't hold the damp. Five of them. The fields are thick with rabbits; you'll not have to go far."
quests.progress: "Five. Coneys are small; I need all five."
quests.complete: "Five, and not a tear in them." Maud stretches each skin over her knee and pins it. "Nettie, the waxed thread." The scrip she hands over is lined in soft grey fur and smells of beeswax. "Keep the salt dry and it'll keep your meat. That's the whole of cooking, my mother said."

steps.text: Bring five coney skins to Maud Tanner at her shop by the South road.

objectives.say: Put them in a pile. I'll count them.

quests.title: Ore Wants a Stout Bag
quests.summary: Bring Maud Tanner three boar hides. Wild boar root in the Mastwood, in the Southwood and at the wallow south of Withy pool. She keeps shop by the South road, 9 to 12 and 2 to 6.
quests.offer:
"If you've been at the seams with a pick, you'll have worn through a sack already. Ore eats leather."

"Boar hide is the only thing that stands up to it. Three of them, and I'll double them into an ore-poke. Mind the tusks. Fen came back from the Mastwood with a hole in his leg once, and he's never let me forget it."
quests.progress: "Three boar hides. The boars won't come to you. Well, they might, and then you'll wish they hadn't."
quests.complete: Maud has to lean her weight on the awl to get it through. "Doubled, and the seams turned in where the stone can't get at them." She draws the thong tight and drops the poke on the counter with a thump. "That'll hold a hundredweight of copper and outlast us both."

steps.text: Bring three boar hides to Maud Tanner at her shop by the South road.

objectives.say: On the floor with them, they'll ruin the counter.

quests.title: Bears in the Hazels
quests.summary: Bears have come down off Crowsfoot Ridge into the hill hazels, an old one with them. Garet wants them gone before they find the Harrows' pigs.
quests.offer:
Garet Moss is scraping a hide on the rail and doesn't look up. "Bears. Down off the ridge into the hill hazels, east of the Mastwood. They never come this low." He sets the scraper down. "Something up there has them moving. Two young ones, and an old boar the size of a cart. Hazelmaw, my father called him, and my father's been dead twenty years."

"Before they find the Harrows' pigs. Mind the old one: he doesn't bluff."
quests.complete: Garet looks at the claw you bring him a long while. "Hazelmaw. I'll be." He hangs it on the rail with the hides. "Twenty years he kept to the ridge. Whatever moved him, I'd rather it hadn't."

steps.text: Drive the bears out of the hill hazels.

objectives.say: The old bear goes down like a felled tree, and the hazels go quiet around it.
